findings.summary: Residual boundary, disclosed and out of scope rather than a defect: the shipped default worker is a placeholder that sleeps and exits 0 without publishing agent.run.started, so under the live default (TICK_CHANNEL=research:p02-smoke-1dce60) each dispatched card is reclaimed to open by the next tick. This is not the §0 wiring break — N1/N2 prove the runs read is consumed — but the consequence of the real worker being V1/R1b scope (README routes worker dispatch to agent-runtime/subagent-mcp, reachable via TICK_WORKER_RUNNER), and publishing started from the dispatcher was correctly rejected earlier while publishing it from the placeholder would breach the §2 write restriction. Churn is confined to the one channel §2 sanctions and capped by --max-writes 5; the dev-note states the boundary honestly.
